axes.rationale: Baseline is no controls: the DiD identification rests on parallel_trends for the unadjusted outcome, and county/year fixed effects (in TWFE) or the group/period dummies (in OLS) already absorb the relevant level heterogeneity. Time-varying socioeconomic covariates (poverty_rate, unemployment_rate, median_hh_income) are plausible bad controls — they can be mediators of Medicaid expansion's economic effects (expansion can affect local income and employment via the ACA labor-market channel), so adding them risks conditioning on a post-treatment variable. They are included as candidates only to show the ATT is not an artifact of confounding secular trends in local economic conditions, not because they are preferred. Explicitly excluded from any control set: deaths and crude_rate (these are mortality outcomes, not covariates, and county_fips-level mechanical constructs of the panel) and population (reserved as the weighting variable, not a control).

Pinned to the full estimand-defined sample (never-expanders + 2014-expanders, late expanders already excluded per the frozen population definition). This exclusion is a data-construction precondition stated in the estimand ('must be verified that panel is filtered this way'), not a robustness fold — it defines which units belong to the estimand, not an alternative sample restriction. Rejected alternative: trimming counties with high pct_uninsured_moe (ACS margin-of-error-based precision filter) — rejected because (a) it does not test the parallel-trends identification assumption at all, it tests measurement noise, (b) MOE is correlated with county population size and thus outcome-correlated, biasing which counties survive the trim, and (c) it would consume a curve fold better spent on control_set/estimator/weighting, which are the axes where this estimand is actually fragile. Analysts should confirm via the status column that late expanders are dropped before running the curve; this is a precondition check, not a spec-menu axis.

Baseline uses the full available pre-2014 panel window to maximize power for estimating pre-trends and the DiD coefficient. Candidate '3' (restricting to the 3 years immediately preceding 2014) tests sensitivity to the length of the pre-period: a short pre-window guards against long-run pre-trend violations of parallel_trends contaminating the estimate, while the full window uses more data to pin down the counterfactual trend. This directly stress-tests the identification_assumption (parallel_trends), making it a substantively relevant fold.

Pinned at the treatment-assignment level: Medicaid expansion status (never_treated vs. expander) is assigned at the state level, so state_fips is the correct clustering level per the standard DiD/panel convention (Bertrand-Duflo-Mullainathan; Abadie et al. on clustering at the level of treatment assignment). Rejected alternative 1: county_fips — clusters below the assignment level, mechanically understates standard errors and overstates significance; this is a known estimation error, not a defensible robustness variant, so it does not buy a fold. Rejected alternative 2: 'none' (heteroskedasticity-robust only) — ignores within-state serial and spatial correlation in a state-assigned treatment, indefensible for this design. Note: clustering on 'state' (the string label) would be an identical partition to state_fips, so it is not a second distinct level and is not listed separately.

Pinned to true: the frozen estimand's population explicitly defines the comparison group as never_treated=1 counties and requires late expanders (states expanding after 2014) to be excluded from the sample entirely. Setting this to false would admit post-2014 expanders as part of the comparison group, which changes the estimand (control group composition) rather than testing robustness of the same estimand under this control set — it is a different research question, not a curve fold. No alternative level is compatible with the estimand as specified.

Baseline TWFE: county and year fixed effects absorb time-invariant county heterogeneity and common year shocks, the standard DiD implementation for this design. Because late expanders are excluded by construction (see never_treated axis), treatment adoption is effectively a single date (2014) shared across all treated units — this design has no staggered-adoption timing variation, so TWFE does not suffer the negative-weighting bias documented for staggered DiD (Goodman-Bacon, de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfœuille); a Callaway-Sant'Anna-style estimator is unnecessary and outside the supported estimator list regardless. Candidate OLS: the pooled two-way-dummy specification using available columns only — an expansion-group dummy built from never_treated (group = 1 - never_treated) interacted with a post-2014 period dummy built from year (post = year >= 2014), equivalent to a canonical 2x2 DiD via treated_post plus separately estimated group and period main-effect coefficients, contrasted with TWFE's absorption of unit and year heterogeneity via fixed effects rather than explicit dummies. This tests whether the ATT is sensitive to explicit level-effect controls versus fully absorbed fixed effects; no columns beyond year, never_treated, and treated_post are assumed.

Baseline population-weighted per the encoding-rule default, which targets the ATT on persons (a person-weighted average effect) — appropriate if the policy-relevant estimand is the effect on the average uninsured person rather than the average county. Candidate 'none' (unweighted, giving each county equal weight) is a real, decision-relevant alternative because the outcome pct_uninsured is defined and reported at the county level ('İlçe düzeyinde sigortasız nüfus yüzdesi'), so an unweighted county-level ATT is arguably the more literal reading of the stated outcome_unit; large-population and small-population counties can differ systematically in baseline uninsurance and in expansion timing effects, so this fold checks whether the ATT is driven by a few large counties under population weights.

args.overall_rationale: Curve size = n(control_set) x n(sample) x n(pre_period) x n(clustering) x n(never_treated) x n(estimator) x n(weighting) = 3 x 1 x 2 x 1 x 1 x 2 x 2 = 24, at the budget ceiling and not exceeding it. Three axes are pinned because they are fixed by the frozen estimand or by design-level assignment structure rather than being genuinely contestable robustness choices: never_treated (the comparison-group definition is stated explicitly in the estimand and any alternative changes the research question), clustering (state_fips is the treatment-assignment level, a methodological requirement rather than a preference), and sample (the late-expander exclusion is a data-construction precondition to verify, not a fold; a plausible alternative restriction, MOE-based trimming, was considered and rejected as testing measurement noise rather than the parallel-trends identification assumption). The budget is spent on the three axes where this DiD design is most fragile in practice: control_set (3 levels, testing bad-control risk from potentially post-treatment economic covariates), estimator (2 levels, testing TWFE fixed-effects absorption against an explicit two-way-dummy OLS DiD, both using only existing columns and both valid here because late-expander exclusion removes staggered-timing bias concerns), and weighting (2 levels, testing county-level versus population-weighted ATT given the county-level outcome_unit). pre_period additionally varies (2 levels) to directly stress-test the parallel_trends identification assumption via pre-trend window length. Together these axes probe confounding, functional form, aggregation weighting, and identification-window sensitivity, the dimensions most likely to move this ATT estimate, while pinning the assignment-structure axes that are not legitimately contestable.
